item.title: Translations in library catalogues: how to find them?
item.description: arXiv:2610.32176v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In library catalogues based on MARC21 bibliographic metadata schema there are about a dozen data elements that catalogers can utilize to record information about the different aspects of translations: whether or not the edition is a translation, source and target language, title of the original work, translator and other contributors, publication data of the original work, literary genre. Libraries however rarely explore the full arsenal, thus to find translation is not a trivial task. The paper describes these important MARC21 data elements, and shows a use case of finding translations in five catalogues (of the Norwegian, Croatian, Polish, Belgian and Dutch national libraries) explaining the differences among the practices, and the results.
item.dc:creator: P\'eter Kir\'aly

item.title: Tampered ML: Evaluating LLM Judgment of Machine Learning Research
item.description: arXiv:2610.32114v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: One approach to accelerating progress on AI alignment is to automate parts of alignment research itself. Doing so requires systems that can perform reliably on hard-to-supervise research tasks, including identifying flaws in research proposals and evaluating whether a proposed experiment supports its intended claim. To evaluate this capability, we introduce Tampered ML, a benchmark of 1,858 item-pairs, each consisting of an experiment proposal reconstructed from a published machine learning paper and a minimally edited counterfactual that introduces a targeted methodological flaw. Models must identify the more methodologically sound proposal in both presentation orders. A human validation study on a stratified sample estimates that 86% of items are valid (95% CI: 81-91%). Frontier models perform above chance but remain far from reliable (with Opus 5 achieving 77.9% accuracy). They are highly sensitive to the order of presentation and favor flawed designs that appear more specific, transparent, or conventional.
item.dc:creator: Soroush Ebadian, Parand A. Alamdari, Joe Benton, Hailey Joren
